answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may post jobs or earn reputation. The registry counts active stake, not names, so splitting capital among a thousand accounts does not multiply influence; each account’s weight remains capped by its deposit. A zenith of activity or a mirror-like cluster of profiles earns no extra trust. To overwhelm the system, a falcon attacker must tie up real capital in every identity, risking forfeiture for abuse and losing access to those funds while the lock lasts.
